messages:
maria: ran a micro-bench today — seeing kernel arbiter choose Triton for seq<=96, then switch to CUTLASS at 128 on A100. tail latency for batch=1 replies jumps ~2.1x.

ashok: that sounds bad. is it from TF32 vs FP16 path or from tile/warp selection?

maria: logs point to different kernel ids. profiler snippet:
```
SEQ=96 kernel=triton_fwd_k1 ms=1.2
SEQ=128 kernel=cutlass_fwd_k4 ms=2.6
```
KV cache warm state. batch=1, kv_cache_hit_rate ~0.92.

tim: are these runs with continuous batching enabled? with small batches batching/hysteresis can amplify switches.

maria: yes `continuous_batching=true`, probe plan enabled. interestingly when kv_cache is empty the switch doesn't happen — looks seq-dependent + kv cache size.

julia: do we have arch tags? A100 vs H100?

maria: A100 for this run. on H100 the Triton kernels are consistently better; CUTLASS only wins on A100 past ~120 tokens.

perf-bot: scheduled job 1765432000 completed. link: https://ci.redwood/bench/1765432000

ashok: hypothesis: kernel selector uses peak-GFlop heuristic that ignores memory traffic from KV cache causing misprediction when kv cache contributes to memory-bound behavior.

tim: agree. propose adding a memory-bandwidth-aware cost term and a hysteresis window on seq-length boundaries. e.g., require N requests over threshold before switching.

maria: quick patch trial: add 10% mem term and hysteresis count=3. results:
```
SEQ=96 -> triton ms=1.25
SEQ=128 -> triton ms=1.4 (no switch)
```
tail latency improved, but avg token throughput down ~3% for long-seq workloads.

julia: tradeoff ok for latency-sensitive customers. we should gate by profile: customer can opt for latency-first vs throughput-first.

ashok: also document fallback: if Triton kernel fails (OOM or launch error) fallback to cuda/cutlass path; but need graceful kv cache transfer. currently we rebuild KV cache on fallback causing ~50ms spike.

maria: added a lightweight memcpy path to copy kv cache pointers so fallback doesn't tear down context. initial tests reduce spike to ~6ms.

tim: can we add a small probe plan that runs 1 warm request every X mins to keep preferred kernel hot? but careful with cost.

julia: add feature flag `kernel_probe_rate` per deployment. default off for Dedicated customers.

maria: I'll open a PR with selector changes, hysteresis, mem term, and probe flag. will include a canary rollout to 5% of reqs.

ashok: ping when PR is up. let's also add a perf regression alert for tail-p95 delta > 20% after rollout.

maria: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/+/1234

perf-bot: canary rollout to 5% started.

tim: thanks. follow-up: add an eval prompt set to reproduce kv-cache-heavy short replies.

julia: assigned to @maria and @ashok.

maria: noted, will post benchmark results in #eng-runtime later.
